target.title: fix: Linux SIGILL during timezone resolution on non-FHS systems (fixes #2127)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #2127 

- Bootstrap timezone discovery before the Linux CLI enters Commander/Foundation-dependent setup.
- When `TZ` is unset and `/etc/localtime` is readable, direct Swift Foundation to the system timezone file.
- Preserve all explicitly configured `TZ` values.
- Add focused Linux regression coverage for fallback and no-op behavior.

## Problem

On NixOS, running a provider usage command with `TZ` unset terminates the process with `SIGILL` (#2127):

```console
$ codexbar usage --provider claude
fish: Job 1, "codexbar usage --provider claude" terminated by signal SIGILL (Illegal instruction)
```

This reproduced with:

- both v0.42.1 Linux x86_64 release artifacts (glibc and musl);
- an unmodified build of `main` at `c852c135`;
- NixOS 26.05 with `/etc/localtime` pointing into the Nix store; and
- no conventional `/usr/share/zoneinfo` directory.

Debugger inspection reaches Swift Foundation timezone conversion around `TimeZone._cfObject`, where execution ends at an intentional `ud2` trap.

## Root cause

Swift Foundation attempts to resolve the process default timezone through conventional Linux zoneinfo locations. NixOS uses a non-FHS layout: the valid system timezone is available through `/etc/localtime`, which points to timezone data in the Nix store.

When `TZ` is absent, Foundation does not discover that valid configuration and traps while constructing the default timezone.

## Fix

`CodexBarCLI.main()` now performs a small Linux-only timezone bootstrap before argument parsing, Commander descriptor construction, logging, or provider work.

The bootstrap:

- runs only on Linux;
- leaves `TZ` untouched whenever the variable is already present;
- verifies that `/etc/localtime` is readable before using it;
- uses the absolute timezone-file form expected by the supported Linux runtimes; and
- becomes a no-op when no usable fallback is available.

The environment change is process-local. It does not modify system configuration or the environment of the calling shell.

## Regression coverage

`CLITimeZoneBootstrapTests` covers:

- selecting `/etc/localtime` when `TZ` is absent and the file is readable;
- preserving named, empty, and custom-path `TZ` values; and
- declining to set a fallback when `/etc/localtime` is unreadable.

The policy logic is tested as a pure helper so the suite does not mutate process-global environment state or become order-dependent under parallel execution.

## Scope and compatibility

- No provider fetching, authentication, account storage, or parsing behavior changes.
- No dependency, package, toolchain, or release-process changes.
- No macOS behavior changes.
- Conventional Linux distributions continue using their configured system timezone.
- Systems without a readable `/etc/localtime` retain the existing behavior.
- Explicit caller timezone configuration always takes precedence.

## Validation

- [x] `swift test --filter CLITimeZoneBootstrapTests` — 3 tests passed
- [x] `make test` — all 31 Linux test selections passed in 3 groups with no retries or failures
- [x] `./Scripts/lint.sh lint-linux` — portable checks passed; SwiftLint reported 0 violations across 1,425 files
- [x] SwiftFormat 0.61.1 on both changed Swift files — `0/2 files require formatting`
- [x] `swift build -c release --product CodexBarCLI --static-swift-stdlib`
- [x] `--help` and `--version` smoke tests with `TZ` unset
- [x] Affected `usage --provider claude` command on NixOS with `TZ` unset — exited normally and returned usage instead of `SIGILL`
- [x] `make check` passed all relevant checks for the changed files; the full Linux CI lint path also passes.

No UI changes; screenshots are not applicable.
